reviews_5s:
This is a solid, well-made set of mesh strainers. The stainless steel construction feels durable, and the fine mesh works well for everything from rinsing grains to straining sauces or sifting dry ingredients.

The three sizes are practical and cover a wide range of kitchen tasks. They stack easily for storage and clean up without any issues. Overall, this set performs exactly as expected and holds up well with regular use.Yup!… expected this quality in the price was good for this brand now if they hold their solder at the handle over time that would be an extra star, but that’s future knowledge that I don’t have :-)When I received these, used them that day! Quality looks fine and for the price, you can’t beat it!Mesh size is perfect, handles are a good length and design. Very versatile for different cooking projects.since i have got these i have noticed i strain alot more stuff. they are built good and can handle heat well. the 3 different sizes really come in handy depending on what i need to strain. very light weight.You cannot have a kitchen without these.I mainly bought them for the brand name and the Made well and durable and a decent value too.I bought these metal strainers to replace a set of silicone strainers I was not happy with. Although the silicone strainers are collapsable, they're not easy to keep clean. When collapsed, the silicone strainers take up a similar amount of cupboard space as the metal ones do. Plus, when baking the metal strainer is bette at sifting flour than the silicone.May with good quality material, easy to grip love the different sizesGood price for this 3 piece strainer set. Works fine.
reviews_1s: The reviews for this three pack of strainers were all mostly positive. Honestly, they were what convinced me to make this purchase! unfortu Unfortunately, I am not impressed. I do like the fact that they are made of stainless steel but that’s as far as it goes. The large strainer rolls all around the countertop, spilling its contents. I tried to push down on the strainer and flatten the bottom so it would stop moving, but that didn’t work. It just pops back out into its original shape. When I rinse berries, I have to carefully prop the long, unwieldy handle up against the windowsill or the coffee maker so that the berries don’t spill out. It’s pretty annoying and my husband refuses to use it. This is not a win!These are trash, plain and simple, period! I know for the price point, you get what you pay for, right? But what (albeit mildly) surprises me is Cuisinart put their name on these, and that's the hook! You see that name and you know (that long ago) this company actually cared about the quality of the product that bore their name. But today's companies are more interested in P&L percentages and who cares weather the actual product is any good. They will squeeze every single penny out of the good name and then squeeze some more. I think it fair to say that as little as 25 years ago, no good company would put out the kind of garbage that is the norm rather than the exception today. Now I'm all for paying a fair price for a fair whatever, and I'm all for a company making a fair profit, even a good profit, that's what makes this country run. But that's all a thing of the past, just like seeing "Made in the US". Ok enough, what makes these trash? The actual strainer part is a seriously thin gauge of cheap metal (I think it is some sort of metal), it almost flexes like a stiff fabric. So too are the rest of the parts and the tiny little welds that hold the handles on fall apart with almost no stress at all. I barely use these because they are so bad and I treat them like eggs when I do use them and they have all fallen apart. Of course, I'm way outside my return window (my fault, I should've sent these back immediately but did not). I foolishly thought that because of the name, they should be ok, even though I kind of know better. I just keep thinking that companies with good names will give you good products. Never again! Caveat Emptor from now on and with everything. But as long as these companies continue to get away with these practices, they have no reason to change and in fact it probable encourages them to push it to the absolute limit. Taking pride in your work...RIP.Quality LOOKS to be good but small food particles get stuck under the rim. Super hard to clean under there. Especially after rinsing something small like quinoa. Not a good design at all. I’d recommend finding another brand. I would not buy again.Junk! The welds broke from the handle to the sifter on the large and middle. Threw them away.I’ve probably used the large strainer a dozen times. After washing it, I gave it a shake to get the water off. The handle popped off where it had been welded. It definitely should not have come apart that easily. Although the materials used to make the strainer seem fine, the quality of the welding job was definitely not good. Disappointing. Now I have a mostly new strainer with no handle.The handle on the small strainer was broken off. The set was supposed to come with a milk nut bag and it wasn't included. The other two strainers are cheaply made and if I put anythi g with any kind of weight in it the handle will break off. Do not buy this brand.Handle pull off on my first use. Poorly weldedRusted already .. my last ones never rustedThe screens on these items are all smashed and out of shape. The small one is not completely attached to the metal frame. Waste of time and money. Would not buy again.I got the delivery this morning. As soon as I opened the mailing bag, I found the item defective. The black dirt and scratches on them are unpleasant and gonna return it.
